bugs.text: A diver that leaves the bottom does not re-enter from the top: makeReturnPath starts at its current position below the screen and curves toward y=-20, so a few frames later it pops back up through the player's row at the same x the dive ended on (within 55 px of the player) and rams the player from below. Unfair, frequent deaths and contrary to the spec's rule.
A Boss shot while diving with two escorts scores 400+400*2 = 1,200 instead of 1,600.
isDiving excludes the 'return' state, so an enemy shot while flying back to its slot scores formation points (50/80/150) rather than dive points.
Entry paths end at the un-swayed slot; on arrival the enemy snaps to the swayed formation position, a jump of up to 16 px for every arriving enemy.
A captured ship is not pulled up the beam; it is created at the player's position and teleports to above the Boss on the next frame.

checkBeamCapture runs every beam frame with no invulnerability check: after captureDualHalf takes one half of a dual fighter, the remaining half is captured by captureSingle on the next frame, which overwrites the first captive (it vanishes) and costs a ship immediately. A freshly respawned blinking ship can also be captured.
The tractor Boss stops at y=100, inside the zako rows (92-108), so it beams from within the formation and overlaps formation sprites instead of hovering partway down the screen.
Dual fighter: when one shot is still on screen, the next press fires a single shot from the empty gap between the two ships (player.x), and up to three shots can be on screen.
During the post-death 'ready' state updateEnemies runs but updatePlayerBullets does not, so enemy bullets hang frozen in mid-air (and divers keep adding frozen bullets) until the player respawns.
sfx.enemyHit is defined but never called; there is no separate enemy-hit sound.
Title prompt reads 'ENTER START' instead of 'PRESS ENTER TO START'.
Boss Galaga only takes escorts from stage 2 onward; on stage 1 bosses always dive alone.

summary: The file is complete, loads clean in the play-test and is organised sensibly: state at the top, one update() dispatching on a state string, one render(), a correct fixed-timestep loop, and pixel-data sprites plus synthesised Web Audio. Nearly every feature in the spec has real, reachable code: curved Bezier entries in groups, sway then breathing, aimed dives with escorts, a widening striped tractor beam with capture, rescue, docking into a dual fighter, hostile captives, challenging stages with wave and PERFECT bonuses, stage flags in arcade denominations, localStorage high score and a hit-ratio results screen. Faithfulness suffers in the details: the sprites are crude blobs with a one-pixel 'flap', enemies snap sideways on arrival, the tractor Boss parks inside the zako rows and the capture teleports rather than pulls, challenge paths are sine sweeps rather than loops, and the two-escort Boss pays 1,200 not 1,600. The one real gameplay defect is the return path: divers that exit the bottom immediately fly back up through the player's row and can ram the ship from below, which the arcade never does and which makes deaths feel unfair. The play-test lost all three ships within about 12 seconds of the first stage (before any dive), which the code does not explain beyond unaimed enemy fire, so the bot's behaviour may be the cause. Overall it plays and looks like Galaga at a glance, with a few rough and unfair edges.
